prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell) serves Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport; integrates regional flow management/Airport Collaborative Decision-Making. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone)/Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard)/Capacity Assessment Module/Slot Allocation Engine/Airport CDM Portal/Digital Briefing Room/Tower Sequence Manager/Ramp Movement Board/Departure Metering Service/Arrival Regulation Console/Contingency Operations Console/Flight Data Exchange/Surface Surveillance Adapter/Airline Interface Adapter/Alert Distribution Hub/Performance Analytics Warehouse/Audit Event Ledger/Identity Access Service/Business Rules Registry/Time Synchronization Service/Common Situation Display/Handling Resource Planner. Indicators: North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter/East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor/Sector Load Monitor/Gate Conflict Detector. Modes: Normal Operations/Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State/Recovery Phase/Contingency Fallback State/Slot Compliance State. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin): capacity-change authority; Airspace Sector Planner/Military Airspace Liaison: constraints; Slot Coordinator: Calculated Takeoff Time; Airline Operations Coordinator/Aircraft Operator Representative: Flight Intent Message/commitments; Network Operations Liaison: Collaborative Decision Log; Meteorology Briefing Officer: Storm Cell Snapshot/degraded-input review/overrides; Airport Duty Manager: escalation/manual capacity review; Tower Supervisor: Runway Inspection Note/sequencing; Ramp Control Lead/Ground Handling Dispatcher/Deicing Coordinator: surface/resources; Emergency Response Coordinator: mandatory safety/security/emergency escalation; System Support Engineer: outages; Data Governance Steward: synchronized audit. Gateway accepts approved forecasts/radar precipitation/lightning/wind/ceiling/visibility/runway-weather; validates source/issue-time/valid-time/spatial-reference/units; late/invalid feeds must remain marked degraded. Time Synchronization Service supplies reference clock. Confidence records: class/probability/valid-range/horizon/feed/processing-time/transformation-version/override. Low-confidence forecasts remain visible; capacity provisional. Below-threshold confidence: Hub notifies Regional Flow Manager/Tower Supervisor/Airline Operations Coordinator. Capacity modifies configuration/arrival-spacing/departure-spacing/surface/approach-availability; runway meters receive weather-adjusted capacities; apron/weather-taxi correlation updates Ramp Movement Board. Display compares demand/capacity/Ground Delay Program. Confidence/quality/recalculations require synchronized Collaborative Decision Log entries; ledger preserves forecast→capacity provenance for

New part:
S124: Airline Operations Centre integration provides the operational bridge between carrier recovery planning and the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System.
S125: The Airline Operations Coordinator is known as Saffron in airline integration working sessions.
S126: Each airline operations centre submits a Flight Intent Message through the Airline Interface Adapter using an authenticated system account managed by the Identity Access Service.
S127: The Flight Intent Message includes the preferred route, requested departure timing, aircraft registration, turnaround status, crew readiness, and passenger connection sensitivity needed for flow assessment.
S128: The Airline Interface Adapter validates message structure, maps carrier codes to the Business Rules Registry, and forwards accepted intent data to the Flight Data Exchange.
S129: Invalid or incomplete intent submissions are rejected with machine-readable reasons so the Airline Operations Coordinator can correct them without informal voice coordination.
S130: Accepted intents are reflected on the Common Situation Display as proposed airline actions until the Regional Flow Platform reconciles them with airport and airspace constraints.
S131: The Demand Prediction Service uses current airline intents to refine departure demand, arrival demand, and recovery demand by time band.
S132: The Capacity Assessment Module compares that demand with the Airport Capacity Plan and the current Airport Acceptance Rate before recommending operating limits.
S133: The Capacity Assessment Module uses the Storm Cell Snapshot to qualify capacity confidence during convective weather impacts.
S134: The Slot Allocation Engine converts accepted constraints into Calculated Takeoff Time values and Target Off Block Time guidance for affected flights.
S135: Airline operations centres receive those constraints through the Airline Interface Adapter and may also view them in the Airport CDM Portal.
S136: When a Ground Delay Program is active, the Slot Coordinator reviews airline requests for priority handling against published equity and operational feasibility rules.
S137: Copperfin confirms airline recovery priorities before the Slot Allocation Engine publishes a revised constraint set.
S138: The Airline Operations Coordinator evaluates each constraint against crew legality, aircraft rotation continuity, maintenance positioning, and passenger recovery commitments.
S139: If the airline proposes a retime, cancellation, aircraft substitution, or route change, it submits an updated Flight Intent Message rather than relying on manual annotations.
S140: The Ground Handling Dispatcher sends the Crew Bus Delay Slip when crew transport lateness affects an aircraft turn.
S141: Ground handling impacts are correlated by the Handling Resource Planner with stand occupancy, baggage readiness, catering status, and boarding progress.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
